newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share trade set to strengthen next week.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share trade set to strengthen next week.

text.p: The Nigerian stock market ended in an optimistic mood on Friday and traders said it was set to maintain the run next week.
The all-share index closed at 8140.50 from 8081.82 on Thursday.
Prices of equities remained on the rise as investors' appetite was unflagging, traders said.
"Some of the gains are artificial, only subsisting because the market lacks depth and breadth," one told Reuters.
Bank shares were gaining from the market perception that they would capitalise to meet a new government directive asking all banks to raise their capital base nine-fold to 500 million naira.
While First Bank touched 16.45 naira on a 15 kobo gain, investors jostling for Union Bank shares paid an additional 40 kobo for it, to close at 14.20 naira.
Oil shares maintained their strong position on growing demand and Agip's full year result which saw profit steady.
Agip closed five kobo higher at 30.25 naira after announcing a 225.1 million naira profit after tax for the year to end-December 1996 against 220.1 million naira a year ago.
Unipetrol added 10 kobo to 75.10 naira, Texaco was 44.30 naira and National Oil ended at 60.00 naira, both rising by 30 kobo.
Computer and office equipment firms were depressed because sellers outnumbered buyers. Thomas Wyatt and WTN fell 10 kobo each to 4.90 naira and 6.45 naira, respectively.
Analysts said shares would remain strong, predicting a relatively trouble-free local government election on Saturday.
They said it was unlikely there would be a breach of security during the poll, which will show whether or not the military rulers are sincere about returning Nigeria to civil rule in 1998.
"The reasons for the current bull run are still operating. As long as they are unchanged equities will remain hot cakes," analyst Ayo Odutayo, said.
